assumptions: The customer's 'functions' means Xano function objects, not endpoints.
30 statements and 3 nesting levels are reasonable limits, borrowed from CONV-040 and CONV-041.
Advisory enforcement is the right starting point for a new policy, per the skill's guidance.
The customer wants a single review-style policy for functions rather than one policy per check; I used REVIEW-001 for the two function rules.
Custom key REVIEW-001 avoids any template prefix collision (REVIEW- is not a template prefix).
workspace_names_used: function kind: acme_sync_shipping_rates (looked at for the giant-function case; not evaluated)
confusions: The skill says to write only names in the catalogue, but stack.size_limit's object_kinds param is not in the catalogue's param list for the check. I used it because the skill's scope section says every check accepts object_kinds, so I'm not certain it's valid for stack.size_limit.

Templates CHG-001 and CONV-040 hardcode object_kinds to query. The skill says to start from the template and change only what the request asks, but the request ('no tests', 'giant functions') does not say endpoints only. I was unsure whether to widen the template or write a separate rule. I kept the template as-is and added a function rule elsewhere.

The skill and catalogue don't say how to combine a template-derived policy with a custom one for the same concern (e.g. two policies both about testing). I avoided duplicating rules but could not confirm the duplicate check would not flag it.

xano policy parse -f summary output omitted the severity line for the medium-severity policies (LOG-010, REVIEW-001) but showed it for the low one (CHG-001). The -o json output shows severity medium as stored, so the summary view appears to hide it. Not blocking, but confusing when checking the file.
The brief says to read the policies/ directory for workspace conventions, but the workspace has no policies/ directory and no policies, so there were no conventions to follow.
wished_for: A recipe for the common code-review complaints (error handling, tests, function size), mapped to checks, so authors don't have to assemble them from templates.
A check or template for error handling in internal logic, not only external calls.
A check that flags tests with no meaningful assertion, or at least a documented limit on what object.test_coverage proves.
Clarification on whether object_kinds is a valid scope param for every check, including stack.size_limit.
A note in the skill on how to combine a template-derived policy with a custom one covering the same concern without tripping policy_duplicate.
why_confidence: The three policies parse, and cover the three named review complaints partly: tests for endpoints and functions, external-call error handling, and function size. But the customer's goal is 'stop juniors breaking prod', which no check measures, and the policies are advisory and unrun, so I haven't seen which objects fail. Error handling and test quality are only partly covered, and the size limit is statement-based rather than line-based.
